people.summary: Teacher, gardener, and keeper of family letters.

Samuel documented ordinary family life with a small camera and labeled most prints with dates and places.
Morgan began interviewing relatives and organizing the photographs inherited from Eleanor and Samuel.
Jordan contributed travel journals, maps, and annotated albums to the collection.

people.summary: Engineer, amateur astronomer, and careful keeper of family records.
people.biography: Anton grew up near a busy freight line and learned to draw machines before he learned to name them. A box of pencil diagrams survives with notes in three languages. His work took him between workshops, bridges, and signal stations, while at home he kept a precise ledger of repairs, birthdays, weather, and visitors. After retiring, Anton recorded neighbors’ memories and made star charts for his grandchildren; those notebooks now sit beside the family photographs.

storyChapters.title: Early years & education
storyChapters.summary: A visual thinker who learned by drawing machines, maps, and constellations.
storyChapters.body: Anton’s earliest notebooks combine mechanical diagrams with observations of the night sky. Teachers remembered his patience with difficult problems, while relatives remembered that he could repair a clock with improvised tools. His education moved between practical workshops and formal engineering study, giving him a habit of explaining complex systems with simple drawings.

storyChapters.title: Family life
storyChapters.summary: Letters, ledgers, and small rituals made the household archive.
storyChapters.body: Anton and Lidia kept a household ledger that began as a list of repairs and gradually became a record of birthdays, visitors, weather, and family decisions. Anton wrote short captions on the backs of photographs and saved cards in envelopes by year. The family remembers him as quiet in crowds and intensely curious at the kitchen table.

storyChapters.title: Engineering career
storyChapters.summary: Field work and research shaped the way Anton recorded the world.
storyChapters.body: His professional life moved between inspection trips, drafting rooms, and a small research group. He kept copies of bridge sketches and signal diagrams, not as trophies but as reminders of what had changed. Colleagues valued his ability to notice a small fault before it became a large one.

storyChapters.title: Later years
storyChapters.summary: Retirement opened time for gardens, star charts, music, and oral history.
storyChapters.body: In retirement Anton built a modest garden observatory and made seasonal star charts for the children around him. He repaired radios, tuned an old piano, and recorded neighborhood stories on a portable cassette deck. His later notebooks are less technical and more personal, filled with names, jokes, weather, and questions he wanted to ask.

storyChapters.title: What remains
storyChapters.summary: A connected collection of people, objects, and memories.
storyChapters.body: The surviving collection brings together photographs, working papers, audio memories, and the small labels that connect them. Some dates are exact; others are estimates based on captions or recollections. The archive preserves both the objects and the uncertainty around them so future family members can continue the research.
